payload.summary: 3 independent QA verify-committed sub-agents (task ids a75975f76a59000be, a20a3b47a4334271a, plus one more referenced inline) reported lost/overwritten notebook cycle entries on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/qa.md within a single dev-team tick (2026-08-06T09:37Z), all self-recovered via git log/re-append, zero permanent data loss.
payload.root_cause_hypothesis: Router dispatched a 9-way concurrent QA fan-out this tick via the newly-shipped Review-Lane QA-Drain Head-Decoupled Invocation (QA_CAP=10). The notebook-write convention (feedback_agent_notebook: 'cycle log, full overwrite') is a read-modify-overwrite pattern with no locking -- safe for 1 writer per tick, unsafe when N=9 same-role agents write the same file concurrently. One agent additionally reported a PostToolUse formatter hook rewriting the file mid-session.
evidence: a75975f76a59000be (FFLOW-STALE-0723-A-VPS-FIX): 2 consecutive lost-update races, resolved via >> append + explicit-pathspec commit on 3rd attempt

a20a3b47a4334271a (FIX-AUDITOR-A30-VMHWM-VETO-TAUTOLOGY): cycle-500/501/502 entries vanished between initial and final read, recovered from git log, attributed a PostToolUse formatter hook rewrite mid-session
a53e0bbd01ff0caa8 / a8ad4a5da85831c8d also noted peer commits sweeping their qa.md contributions (benign convergence, not data loss, but same shared-hot-file pattern)
payload.suggested_fix_direction: Either (a) serialize notebook-write via a task_claim mutex per notebook file before the read-modify-overwrite, or (b) change the convention from full-overwrite to append-only for the cycle-log section so concurrent writers cannot clobber each other, or (c) cap same-tick same-role concurrent fan-out below N where this becomes observable. Router defers the actual design to po/architect.
